title: Microinjection of Western Corn Rootworm, Diabrotica virgifera virgifera, Embryos for Germline Transformation, or CRISPR/Cas9 Genome Editing
protocol: Obtain WCR adults (500 - 1,000) from a reliable source.
Place WCR adults in a 30 cm³ cage.
Prepare WCR artificial diet according to manufacturer's protocol.
Pour a 1 cm-thick layer of prepared diet into a 38 oz container.
Store unused diet at 4 °C for up to 2 months.
Put a Petri dish (100 x 15 mm) with adult diet (10 - 15 g) into the cage.
Add more diet when food is low or dry.
Place a flask (300 mL) with water, covered by a cotton ball, in the cage for moisture.
Change water when it runs low.
Maintain WCR at 26 °C with 60% humidity and a 14:10 light cycle.
Make an egg collection chamber using 1% agar in water in a sterile Petri dish (100 x 15 mm²).
Store the egg collection chamber at 4 °C after agar solidifies.
Place a single layer of filter paper followed by four layers of cheesecloth on the surface of the agar for egg collection.
Place egg collection plate into WCR cage late in the day.
Cover egg collection plate with a tinfoil tent.
Remove egg collection chamber around 8 or 9 A.M.
Pick up one layer of cheesecloth at a time using forceps and place it in a beaker of water.
Gently stir to wash eggs off cheesecloth.
Transfer washed eggs from the first beaker to another beaker of water using a bulb pipette.
Repeat washing steps 2-3 times.
Transfer cleaned eggs onto filter paper using a bulb pipette, minimizing water carry-over.
Cut black filter paper into strips as wide as a glass slide.
Tape the filter paper strips firmly to the glass slide to ensure they lay flat.
Apply non-toxic glue in fine lines on the filter paper, ensuring lines are thinner than egg diameter.
Use a fine brush to gently move WCR eggs one by one from their original position to the glue line.
Place each egg on the glue before it dries out.
Maintain at least one egg's distance between each egg.
Prepare high-quality supercoiled plasmid DNA using an endotoxin-free commercial kit.

Combine helper plasmid at a final concentration of 250 ng/μL with donor plasmid at a final concentration of 750 ng/μL and phenol red buffer at a final concentration of 20% to prepare the injection solution.
Vortex the prepared solution briefly.
Centrifuge the solution for 3 min at maximum speed to precipitate particles that could clog the needle.
Pull borosilicate glass needles using a Flaming/Brown type micropipette puller.
Secure pulled needles on double-sided sticky tape in a Petri dish or other clear container.
Backfill the injection needle by using a micro-loader tip to pipet 0.5 - 1.0 µL down inside the needle near the tapered end.
Remove bubbles from the tip of the needle if any occur.
Insert the injection needle into the needle holder.
Open the tip of the needle by gently breaking with a fine pair of forceps or touching/dragging the tip on the coverslip or glass slide.
Wet the surface of 1 - 3 eggs with sterile water using a fine paintbrush.
Insert the needle and inject the solution before the surface dries.
Look for the appearance of a small amount of red color inside the eggs during injection to indicate successful microinjection.
Crush or remove any damaged, empty, or otherwise uninjectable eggs.
Place the filter paper on the surface of a 1% agar dish after all eggs are injected.
Seal the dish with plastic paraffin film and place it in a 26 °C insect rearing incubator for 12 days.
Mix paraffin film with agar dishes to prevent cross-contamination of mold between dishes.
Start checking embryos for newly-hatched larvae 12 days post-injection.
Continue daily checks for the next 2 weeks to monitor hatching.
Transfer larvae using a fine brush to a rearing box containing sprouted corn and soil.
Rear larvae at 26 °C following standard WCR rearing methods.
